# Provenance and reproducible parity

Design-system source: byteowlz/design-system
`0968afc89e0919ce856a4d99351bc475b26a87ee`.
Reference copies: spec roles/radius/slots/Base16 policy; shadcn-ts
roles/derive-base16/color/radius. Roles are data-extracted, not a new mapping.
License declaration: preserved reference/package.upstream.json (MIT); LICENSE
supplies that text/attribution. No spec or authored token value is changed.

Studio source: byteowlz/design-studio
`c008b88a32d61d98563ce464c861f98d58e569e7`.
The six data/schemes house inputs are exact copies of generated/oqto-web/schemes;
Nord is an exact shadcn-ts source copy under its scheme ID filename.
reference/studio-color.py.txt supplies the observed f32 conversion contract.
reference/studio-omarchy.py.txt documents Studio's data-only ANSI output.
Studio is byteowlz first-party source; no third-party Omarchy code is copied.
The Omarchy input map data is extracted from templates webapp script at
`6c6214ec1acd3fb0a8bdf8ca805196d564c57593`; unchanged source is archived
in reference/templates-omarchy.mjs.txt for drift inspection only, never execution.
Archived source has a .txt suffix to prevent accidental runtime execution or
mistaking provenance copies for additional production implementations.

testdata/parity.json is generated by running the pinned Studio color parser
over the input scheme/role data and canonical widening recipes. It records
concrete sRGB slot/role values, not a second runtime engine.
`uv run --script scripts/reference-parity.py` reproduces the golden without
services or machine-local paths. Inspect hash changes before accepting drift.
reference/hashes.json locks inputs/reference/golden bytes, and Go tests compare
the role table with the archived canonical TypeScript table. Hash validation
does not prove provenance on its own; source revisions and copied bytes are
the audit trail.

No native/window/platform or hardware certification follows from these parity
tests. MyGo is pinned v0.3.2 (MIT dependency, protected by go.sum).
